indicators.flag: A customer or a customer’s counterparty conducts transactions with OFAC-designated entities and individuals, or transactions that contain a nexus to identifiers listed for OFAC-designated entities and individuals, to include, email addresses, physical addresses, phone numbers, or passport numbers, or virtual currency addresses.
indicators.red_flag: OFAC-designated counterparty / identifier match (email, phone, passport, VC address)
indicators.rationale: OFAC sanctions screening against designated-entity identifiers is a baseline control a mid-size US bank already runs on payment and account data.

indicators.flag: Information included in a transaction between customers indicates support for terrorist campaigns.
indicators.rationale: Detecting terrorist-campaign support encoded in free-text memo or messaging fields requires external interpretation context that core structured transaction data does not supply.

indicators.flag: A customer conducts transactions with a Money Services Business (MSB) or other financial institution, including one that offers services in virtual currency, operates in higher-risk jurisdictions tied to Hamas activity, and is reasonably believed or suspected to have lax customer due diligence (CDD) requirements, opaque ownership, or otherwise fails to comply with anti-money laundering/combatting the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) best practices.
indicators.red_flag: Counterparty MSB/FI in Hamas-tied high-risk jurisdiction with weak AML/CFT
indicators.rationale: Counterparty-MSB and high-risk-jurisdiction flags are partly visible in wire routing, but judging another institution's CDD quality and opaque ownership needs cross-institution attribution the bank only partly holds.

indicators.flag: A customer conducts transactions that originate with, are directed to, or otherwise involve entities that are shell corporations, general “trading companies,” or other companies that have a nexus with Iran or other Iran-supported terrorist groups, such as Hizballah and Palestine Islamic Jihad.8
indicators.red_flag: Shell / "trading company" counterparty with Iran / Hizballah / PIJ nexus
indicators.rationale: Attributing a counterparty as a shell or front company with an Iran/Hizballah/PIJ nexus depends on external sanctions-network and adverse-media intelligence not present in transaction data.

indicators.flag: A customer that is a charitable organization or nonprofit organization (NPO)9 solicits donations but does not appear to provide any charitable services or openly supports Hamas’s terrorist activity or operations.  In some cases, these organizations may post on social media platforms or encrypted messaging apps to solicit donations, including in virtual currency.
indicators.red_flag: NPO soliciting donations with no apparent charitable services / Hamas support
indicators.rationale: Establishing that an NPO solicits but provides no services or openly backs Hamas requires external NPO-sector and social-media adverse-media attribution outside the bank's data.

indicators.flag: A customer that is a charitable organization or NPO receives large donations from an unknown source over a short period of time and then sends significant wire transfers or checks to other charitable organizations or NPOs.
indicators.red_flag: NPO large inbound donations → rapid pass-through to other NPOs
indicators.rationale: The rapid large-inflow-then-pass-through-to-other-NPOs pattern is a pure velocity-and-flow signature fully observable in the bank's own wire and check data, yet is not flagged by today's rules.

build_logic.logic: On an NPO-classified account, flag when large aggregate inbound donations from a small/unknown set of sources are followed within the window by significant outbound wires or checks to other NPO/charity counterparties, where outbound-to-NPO ratio exceeds threshold and dwell time is short.
build_logic.source: core wire transfer + check clearing + account-classification (NPO) data
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → NPO pass-through review gate

indicators.flag: A customer conducts transactions with known or suspected virtual currency addresses tied to terrorism or terrorist financing donation campaigns.
indicators.red_flag: Counterparty VC addresses tied to terror-financing donation campaigns
indicators.rationale: Matching transactions to virtual-currency addresses tied to terror-financing campaigns needs crypto chain-analytics enrichment layered on top of the bank's own on/off-ramp records.
